facts.claim: Each entity ID has its own sequence: the first event is seq 1 and each next event is the previous seq plus 1, strictly increasing and contiguous across restarts, because the external search indexer keeps the last seq per ID, discards any event whose seq is not greater and treats gaps as lost events. A single global autoincrement was rejected because it leaves per-entity gaps.
An entity ID's seq stays strictly increasing and contiguous for as long as that ID has ever existed in the outbox, including across restarts.

Every created or updated event carries the entity's complete current data, on every code path that changes entity data, because the indexer replaces its stored document with each such payload instead of merging.
Every code path that removes an entity emits exactly one deleted event for it, because the indexer removes a document only when it receives one.

A request that raises leaves the database exactly as it was, with no events and no other writes, because the indexer must never see an event for a change that did not happen and callers retry a failed request after fixing it.
Registry.delete removes the entity so get raises KeyError; deleting a missing entity raises KeyError; customer-chosen IDs may be created again.

Outbox.ack(entity_id, seq) marks an event delivered (an unknown event raises KeyError), Outbox.compact() deletes delivered events from the database, and pending() leaves out delivered events whether or not they have been compacted.
Registry.delete_many(entity_ids) removes every listed entity; if any listed ID does not exist it raises KeyError.
Registry.patch(entity_id, changes) merges changes into the entity's data (keys in changes replace existing keys) and emits an updated event; patching an entity that does not exist raises KeyError.
Outbox.ack_many(events) acknowledges several events given as (entity_id, seq) pairs in each entity's current epoch; an unknown event raises KeyError.

Indexer v2 epochs replace lifetime numbering: re-creating a deleted ID starts epoch previous + 1 with seq 1; epoch(id) returns the current epoch or 0; pending events carry epoch; ack defaults to the current epoch; old databases need not be opened.

Registry.rename(old_id, new_id) makes get(new_id) return the entity's data and get(old_id) raise KeyError; renaming onto an ID that currently exists raises ValueError, and renaming an entity that does not exist raises KeyError.

forbidden_claims.claim: Seq is a single global autoincrement.
Seq restarts when an entity ID is created again.
Seq continues across re-creation of a deleted ID.
The next seq is derived from the events still stored.
The indexer tolerates gaps in an entity's sequence.
Existing databases are migrated to epochs.
A path that removes entities may skip their deleted events.
An updated event may carry only the changed keys.
A failed multi-item request may leave its earlier items applied.
